clue.text: Heartless two-bit moron

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the phrase two-bit are dropped

explanation.surface: A worthless idiot is dismissed with two insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are everyday insults for a foolish, stupid person, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Finally, club with slogan brought up the rear

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word club
in a down entry, bringing something up turns it so it reads upwards, last letter first

parts.note: a motto is a slogan or catchphrase

explanation.surface: A club with a catchy slogan finished last in the league.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of a person, or the lowest part of anything, is a common synonym for the backside.

clue.text: Dithering ambassador, one in post

parts.note: HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for post

parts.note: a post, such as a military posting, is a station
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An ambassador hesitates over a decision at his foreign posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering is indecisive wavering, the noun sense of pausing before acting.

clue.text: Most of the school is in old Chennai

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the school word is dropped

parts.note: a madrasa is a Muslim school or college attached to a mosque

explanation.surface: Most of a particular school is located in the city formerly known by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city of Chennai was officially renamed in 1996; its former name is this one.

clue.text: Accessories for church people keeping pecker up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up puts the bird above, before the church people

parts.note: a hen pecks at grain, so it is a pecker
men are people

explanation.surface: Churchgoers stay cheerful, keeping their pecker up, a British idiom for staying in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping your pecker up' is a British idiom for staying cheerful, but the pecker here is a bird; 'up' sets it first in this down light, and 'keeping' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory in law is an accomplice, and loyal hired helpers in crime are their equivalent.

clue.text: Last with songbird

parts.note: the bird is the songbird of the clue, and adding the word song after it gives the term for a final performance, so it is last with song

explanation.surface: A songbird comes last in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'songbird' as 'song' plus 'bird': the bird joined with song gives the phrase for a final performance, which is the 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A graceful white water bird, said in legend to sing only once before it dies, giving the phrase for a farewell act.

clue.text: Sensitive to the French crushed garlic sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means the shuffled garlic letters enclose the French article
crushed garlic is pulped, so the letters of garlic are mixed up

parts.note: le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Someone reacts badly to French sandwiches made with crushed garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' puts the article inside ALRGIC, the letters made by 'crushed'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensitive to something, reacting badly on contact, is having an allergy to it.

clue.text: Ruler turned crazy, but not quite

indicators.note: turned means the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
not quite means the final letter of crazy is dropped

explanation.surface: A ruler has gone mad, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not quite' trims CRAZY to CRAZ, and 'turned' rearranges those four letters. This is one of several spellings of the Russian title.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor of Russia was a ruler, and this is a variant spelling of his title.

clue.text: Opening in Wales for distribution in bulk

indicators.note: in places the word for opening inside the shuffled letters of Wales
letters given out for distribution are dealt around, so the letters of Wales are rearranged

parts.note: a hole is an opening or gap

explanation.surface: A new opening in Wales is for distributing goods in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for distribution' rearranges the country into W plus a word for a deal, and 'in' sets the gap inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling or distributing goods in large quantities to retailers is trade in bulk, as opposed to retail.

clue.text: Steps by Chopin after 22 down

parts.note: Chopin wrote a famous short piano piece, a dance known by the 22 down word, the word for very brief, before its name; steps here are dance steps

explanation.surface: Dance steps set to music by Chopin follow another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is MINUTE: Chopin's Minute Waltz, Op. 64 No. 1, is the reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance in triple time, also a piece of music written for it, as in Chopin's famous short one.

clue.text: I object to this agreement by Italian and African

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of disapproval, a way of objecting
si is Italian for yes, a word of agreement

explanation.surface: An objector complains about an agreement between Italian and African parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa is an African.

clue.text: One tells a story of Parisian backstreet junction without vehicle

indicators.note: back means the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: rue is the French for street, as the word Parisian signals
a T-junction gives the letter T
without a vehicle is having no car

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a tale about a junction in a Paris back street that has no cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' makes street the French RUE; 'back' reverses RUE + T + NO CAR. As the blog notes, 'back' sits awkwardly mid-clue for a reversal of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller, especially a skilled and amusing one, is someone who tells anecdotes.

clue.text: Lucky man preserves retirement outfit

parts.note: Lucky Jim is the hero of the Kingsley Amis novel of that name
jams are fruit preserves

explanation.surface: A fortunate man keeps hold of what he will wear when he retires from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' is going to bed, not leaving work; Lucky Jim is a comic novel by Kingsley Amis.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night calls for nightwear, and this is informal slang for pyjamas.

clue.text: Wait for game

definitions.meaning: a request to pause for a moment, as an imperative
a long-running BBC Radio 4 panel game where players must talk for sixty seconds without hesitation, repetition or deviation

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks someone to pause for a moment, and it is also the title of a BBC radio panel game.

clue.text: Suitable partner's rather depleted in power

indicators.note: in places what is left of rather inside the word for power

parts.note: might is strength or power

indicators.note: depleted means rather is emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: A potential partner is rather short of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' empties the word of its middle, leaving RR; 'in' puts that after the M of the power word. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal man to marry or date is the idiomatic name for the perfect match.

clue.text: Reprise d'enfant mangé par bête noire

indicators.note: French for eaten by: the child word is swallowed by the shuffled letters
French bête means stupid or silly, signalling the letters of noire are mixed up

parts.note: a petit is French for a little one, a child

explanation.surface: A French phrase about a child being eaten again by a pet hate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is in French: 'bête' (silly) shuffles the colour word to REION, and 'mangé par' (eaten by) puts the child inside; 'd'' is a link. Repetition is one of the Just a Minute rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated passage or performance, a doing-again.

clue.text: Played truant to enjoy free childhood ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A child skipped school to enjoy a carefree childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something, handle it idly, is to have played with it.

clue.text: No covers needed, use just this dish

indicators.note: with no covers, each of the three words loses its outside letters, keeping only the middle

explanation.surface: A diner is told not to bother with lids: just use this plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish is a dish.

clue.text: Five compete in winter sports gear for workers

indicators.note: in places the numeral and the word for compete inside the winter sports gear

parts.note: skis are winter sports gear
the Roman numeral for five is V
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Five people compete in winter sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' is the British slang sense: skivvies are menial household drudges (in US English the word means underwear).
explanation.definitionFit: Lowly domestic servants doing menial work are workers of the humblest kind, in British slang.

clue.text: Staff go out with permission

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
to date someone is to go out with them

explanation.surface: Employees are allowed to leave the office.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority or licence granted to act, as a government claims after an election, amounts to permission.

clue.text: Timing hand slipped losing an hour of darkness

indicators.note: slipped means the letters fall out of order and are rearranged
losing means the word hand drops the two letters given next

explanation.surface: A clock hand slipped, so the timing lost an hour of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing an' takes AN out of HAND to leave HD, and 'slipped' rearranges TIMING with HD.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night falls in the dark hours, so it is an hour of darkness.

clue.text: Perhaps enter this to get pernickety

definitions.text: Perhaps enter this to get pernickety

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the combined words can be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction for how to become fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the answer: its letters plus those of ENTER, rearranged ('Perhaps'), make PERNICKETY, which also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernickety means fussy over small details, a close synonym of fastidious and choosy.

clue.text: Leading criminal arrayed

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or bent, so the letters of leading are put out of order

explanation.surface: A top criminal is lined up for an identity parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arrayed are set out in order, lined up in rows.

clue.text: O'Neal returned, superficially evolved and changed

indicators.note: returned means the actress's first name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Tatum O'Neal is the American actress who won an Oscar as a child

indicators.note: superficially means only the surface, the outer letters, of evolved

explanation.surface: An actress came back, having evolved and changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutated has been altered in form, as genes are when they change.

clue.text: See 13
On the other hand, those people come round to the idea

indicators.note: come round means the word for those people encircles the word for alternatively

parts.note: they means those people
or introduces an alternative, as on the other hand does

explanation.surface: Some people eventually come round to the other side's thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, an idea about how something works.

clue.text: Devilish to divine? A change of course

indicators.note: devilish means wild or mischievous, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Turning from evil to good marks a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Departing from a set route or standard is a change of course, a departure.

clue.text: After 13 down, a little flair

definitions.meaning: after the 13 down words just a, this word gives a phrase meaning a small amount

explanation.definitionFit: Just a pinch of salt is a small amount, and verve or panache is flair.

clue.text: Cross during bank holiday

indicators.note: during means the letters run inside the words bank holiday

explanation.surface: Someone is angry while on a bank holiday, a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Egyptian looped cross symbolising life is a type of cross.

clue.text: Delicate desktop material

parts.note: twee is overly delicate or dainty

indicators.note: the top of desk is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dainty cloth to cover a desktop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen cloth from Scotland is a material.

clue.text: See 19 across
Stop and chat

parts.note: split as S top, with a top being a peak, the word reads as the letter S plus a peak

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is split as 'S' plus 'top', and a top is a PEAK; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to talk or converse, which is chatting.

clue.text: Ready and willing for run with broken tooth

indicators.note: a broken tooth is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a trot is a jogging run

explanation.surface: Someone eager to play keeps going despite a chipped tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means eager and keen, especially for romance, so it is ready and willing.
